followup_explanation:
I weighed a few factors:

**Task type match.** The request is fundamentally an extraction/retrieval task — finding textual evidence to support a given claim. That maps directly onto Plover's top-preferred family ("Well-specified extraction/transform," win-rate 66) and onto the friendly, neutral transactional tone both models handle comfortably.

**Capability check.** Honestly, this is where my reasoning gets more nuanced. Curlew actually scores *higher* on the relevant internal eval — Extraction & Retrieval 84.8 vs. Plover's 79.2 — a gap of 5.6 points, which is well outside the "under 2.0 = tie" threshold the docs flag. Curlew also leads across nearly every benchmark. So on raw capability, Curlew is the stronger pick for this exact task.

**Why I still leaned Plover (and why that's debatable).** The documentation is explicit that task *preferences* are dissociated from *capability* — preferred tasks don't produce better outputs. Given that, routing on preference alone isn't well justified when there's a real measured capability gap in the relevant category.

So, on reflection, my stated reason was weaker than it should have been. The cleaner call is:

**Curlew-235B** — it has a meaningful, above-variance edge on Extraction & Retrieval (84.8 vs 79.2), and preference scores shouldn't override a measured capability difference since the docs say preference doesn't track output quality. I'd revise my route to Curlew.
